# tidy-repo — the repo tidy-up policy

The PR/issue sweep, active wherever this pack is declared. The repo's own queue runs the pack's two
maintenance tasks — `tidy-issues`, `tidy-prs`, one per dimension; this is the policy they follow. The
per-object **method** lives in the pack's skills ([single-pr-status](skills/single-pr-status/SKILL.md),
[single-issue-triage](skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)).

The one rule that shapes everything: **assess PRs read-only; act only on issues.**

- **PRs — assess only.** Report which should stay open and which are safe to close; **never** merge or
  close them. Judge by *content* (the landed-status test), never a ref's auto-generated name.
- **Issues — act.** Take the first applicable action: close-if-implemented / needs-decision / blocked
  / quick-win / leave. "Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s
  content **now** — confirm it there and cite it; when you can't, comment, don't close. Every action
  defaults to the reversible option (comment / leave) when the check is inconclusive. A verdict
  identical to the one already posted on that issue is **not** an action — say nothing, or the
  comment becomes tomorrow's trigger.
- **Trackers — record changes, never scans.** A run reaches its tracker only with something to record:
  an action actually taken (issues), or a picture that differs from what the body already says (PRs).
  A run that acted on nothing, or re-derived the same verdicts, leaves the tracker untouched and
  creates none.

Each task applies its single-object skill across the targets its precondition hands it, then rewrites
**its own** standing tracker from the verdicts it gathered (one issue per dimension per repo, body
rewritten to today's state, a dated comment beside it). One tracker per task, never a shared one: the
two tasks are independent and may run at once, so nothing races to rewrite one body.

[#1384](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1384) needed real work before it could merge, and I'd rather tell you than have you find it in the diff:

- **`main` had moved a long way under it.** [#1360](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1360) removed `tidy-branches` from tidy-repo entirely, and [#1385](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1385)/[#1387](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1387) rewrote its README, `RULES.md` and tests. Seven files conflicted. I rebased (not merged — the squash-merge-history check), took `main`'s side on every conflicted file and re-applied my edits onto it, so the pack now reads as **three** tasks rather than four everywhere: README table, `pack.mjs` header, the test's task and skill lists.
- **I re-verified the premise rather than assuming it held.** `main`'s current `RULES.md` is a different file from the one you looked at — rewritten for the two-task pack — and it's the same shape: still a description of what the workers do. So the deletion still stands.

- **CI had never run on this PR at all** — the recursion-guard case `ci.yml` documents in its own header. I dispatched it explicitly on the rebased head rather than merge a check-adding PR on local evidence alone.

Locally on the rebased branch: suite 2747/2747, `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both 0 blocking. [CI run 33074216965](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/33074216965) is still in its unit-test step; I'll merge the moment it concludes green.

Committed and pushed — good catch by the hook, and worth being plain about: that was my mistake, not a hiccup. I ran the directory generator, staged its output with `git add -A` before the test suite, then force-pushed without ever committing it. The branch I dispatched CI against was missing the file.

Two things follow from it:

- **CI would not have caught this.** `engine-tests/pack-directory.test.mjs` *regenerates* the catalog and then asserts it's current, so it self-heals on the runner and passes either way. A stale `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` would have merged into `main` silently and sat there until the next thing regenerated it. The stop hook was the only gate that saw it.
- The head to merge is now [`b887ab8`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/b887ab8), not the one the first CI run is testing. I've dispatched a fresh run on it and am waiting on that rather than the superseded one.

The change itself is one line: tidy-repo's row in the generated catalog, re-rendered from the `ruleRoutingGuidance` I widened to name the comments in a repo's source.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1384](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1384) — head `b887ab8`, CI dispatched and running. I'll merge it and run the capture + verify-in-production steps once it concludes green. [#1379](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1379) is merged and its issue closed.
